ratings_why.fun: Every tier does its job: Gust Pages win early fights, Föhn and the Heron grow mid-game, the Tower and High Pressure pay off late; ordering puzzles keep each turn live, though permanent growth is thin before Tier 6.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because Late makes the hand a second board that lands mid-fight, out of reach of the enemy's Start of Combat; no current tribe or Battlegrounds tribe plays from the hand during combat.

verdict_why: The core is strong, but what happens when your board empties with Late units still waiting is unwritten, and the whole Late half leans on it.

points.text: Late doesn't say what happens if your board is wiped before your third attack (or before High Pressure's Storm) while Late units wait: does the fight end as a loss, or do they arrive? Say which.
Steward of the Bag of Winds: say whether the repeated Gust counts as a separate Gust for Föhn, Mistral, the Heron, the Glass and the Tower. The counts change a lot either way.
Lady High Pressure: let the Storm also break when your last other unit dies, so a wide enemy can't leave her holding everything when you lose.
Windhover's once-a-fight +1/+1 is the flattest seed; letting it count Gusts beside it, or grow once per Gust up to three, would make it a real Tier 1 seed for the Squall build.
Permanent growth before Tier 6 is mostly Föhn and the Heron; a second Tier 4–5 permanent buffer for the Late build (beyond Black Cloud on arrivals only) would smooth the curve into the late game.

standouts.why: Duke Cumulonimbus grows with how long the fight runs, which makes his arrival timing a real choice against Black Cloud.
Lady High Pressure ties Gust and Late into one capstone with a big, readable payoff moment.
Sir Vane turns play order into a decision from Tier 2 and keeps paying in the Late build.

weakest.why: Windhover grows +1/+1 once a fight; it barely seeds anything.
Keeper of the Glass is a plain threshold gold card that the Steward makes trivial.
Dew-Pond Heron is a generic 'biggest unit grows' buffer that the tribe's Gust count caps quickly.

flags.note: The Tower at eight faces gives +8/+8 to all seven units a turn, about 8 bodies; capped and within the top end, but the hottest permanent card.
Black Cloud with the Wild Hunt gives every revived unit +2/+2 permanently each fight (+4/+4 golden); bounded by deaths, but it adds up over many turns.
High Pressure with the Steward and goldens multiplies held Gusts up to ×9 with Mistral's cleave; fight-only, but one-sided wipes are likely.
Whether a doubled Gust counts twice for Gust counters isn't written.
Like all Late units, what happens if your board is empty before it arrives isn't written.
